title: Per-tenant cost-sculpting heuristics and graceful revert for batching/prefix cache
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Background: Customers with mixed workloads show large variance in per-token costs. We need an automated system that recommends per-tenant and per-route batching and prefix-caching rules tailored to observed request shapes and business tiers. Goal: produce deterministic heuristic recommendations, run safety simulations, and publish reversible config commits with staged observability and automatic rollback on regressions.
Scope: - profiling tenant-level seq-length and concurrency distributions - generate ranked candidate policies (batch size, max latency SLO, allowlist/denylist of routes for prefix cache) - run simulated traffic through runtime cost + quality model - produce a reversible commit that can be staged to canary tenants, measure key metrics, and automatically revert if thresholds breached.
Acceptance Criteria:
- system outputs candidate policies as JSON snippets and an explainability summary for each tenant
- simulation harness runs 30-day synthetic replay and reports delta cost/latency/quality
- commit flow supports staged canary to 5% tenants, 20% and full, with automatic rollback conditions
- all commits create a rollback token and human-facing runbook entry
- dashboards show per-tenant delta cost and error rates within 5 minutes of rollout
comments: 2026-02-22 - Spike complete: profiled 42 internal tenants, found three dominant shapes (short-chat-high-concurrency, long-doc-single-shot, mixed). Riley Chen.

2026-02-28 - Draft heuristic: use percentile-based batch targets (p50/p90) and prefer prefix-cache for routes with >10% repeated prefixes. Added to doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/cost-sculpting-spike
2026-03-03 - Simulation: synthetic replay for tenant T-194 reduced token cost by 18% but increased p95 latency by 12% under naive batching. Need gating rules to cap latency impact. Miguel Santos.

2026-03-07 - Design review with PM and Runtime: agreed to add tier-matrix (free/standard/enterprise) where higher tiers prefer latency SLOs over cost. Design notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-cost-sculpting-design
2026-03-09 - Safety commit prototype: implemented reversible commit token and staged canary pipeline. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8275
2026-03-12 - QA: ran chaos test (node eviction) during canary stage; rollback trigger fired correctly for simulated p95 spike. Pending: add rate-limit hysteresis to avoid flapping. QA lead: Dana Park
2026-03-14 - Blocking: need standardized telemetry tags for per-tenant delta cost and origin of change (heuristic vs manual). Created ENG-531405 to standardize tags. Miguel Santos
simulation_results: tenant-T-194: cost -18% / p95 latency +12% (naive) / after gating: cost -9% / p95 latency +2%
tenant-T-207: cost -6% / p95 latency -1% (prefix-cache applied to search-route)
overall-sample: median cost -7% with latency SLO breaches 1.2% of runs
runbook: Step 1: Generate candidate policies via heuristics-runner (internal CLI) - see README
Step 2: Run simulation harness with tenant replay (30-day) and inspect metrics
Step 3: Create reversible commit using commit-token API and schedule canary (5%/20%/100%)
Step 4: Monitor dashboards for cost delta, p95 latency, error-rate; rollback if latency breach >5% or errors >0.5%
Step 5: If rollback occurs, open incident and tag commit-token with failure reason
